transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Eriksson (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (CTO, QuantaCare), Sara Gomez (Data Privacy Lead), Asha Iyer (Platform), Tom Wu (SRE), Rachel Kim (Product)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
QuantaCare and Redwood ran through POC success criteria for a 6-week pilot focused on telemetry, consent-aware logging, ephemeral prompt retention, and benchmark sizing. The convo centered on what counts as PII, how to toggle ephemeral logging per user consent, real retention windows (24h vs 90d), and how Redwood's private options (VPC/on-prem) affect telemetry. Next steps include sample workload, security checklist, and a 2-day benchmark window.

Topics:
- Consent and ephemeral logs model
- PII detection and redaction pipeline
- Retention windows by data sensitivity
- Prompt storage: hashed-only vs plaintext storage
- Benchmark targets: p95 latency, tokens/sec, 2k rps synthetic run
- Timeline for pilot and what success looks like

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Um, we'll run through the POC scope, the telemetry question, and the retention/consent stuff. Jonas is going to do the technical run-through.
[01:12] Liam O'Neill: Thanks Maya. Quick context — QuantaCare is building a patient-support chat assistant that touches PHI-like fields. We're trying to run a six-week pilot to validate both latency and privacy controls before we roll to a 50k MAU cohort.
[03:05] Sara Gomez: Yeah and on our side privacy is the big gating factor. We need to be able to selectively not persist prompts if the user hasn't consented, and when we do persist it must be redacted and audit logged.
[05:03] Jonas Eriksson: Totally. At a high level Redwood supports a tiered retention model — ephemeral mode (no writes to persistent prompt storage), short-term cache (24h encrypted, auto-evict), and long-term retained for users who opt in. For the pilot we recommend ephemeral default and explicit opt-in for retention.
[07:20] Rachel Kim: When you say ephemeral, is that purely memory KV cache or are you writing to disk temporarily? Because our SRE is worried about crash recovery and replay.
[09:10] Tom Wu: Yeah we have regulatory folks saying we can't lose traces needed for incident investigations. So we need a middle ground.
[11:30] Jonas Eriksson: Right. Ephemeral here means we keep tokens only in RAM / KV cache for the runtime. If a request needs to be retried within the process lifetime it can be replayed from KV. We do not write full prompts to persistent blob storage unless the opt-in flag is set. In the POC we can enable a flagged short-lived encrypted write (24h TTL) to an audit-log bucket that is accessible only by your security team.
[14:05] Sara Gomez: That 24h TTL works for me as an investigation window, but we also need redaction rules for PII. Does Redwood do automatic PII masking?
[15:35] Priya Malhotra: We have a two-stage pipeline. First pass is a heuristic redactor (regex + NER) that runs pre-send. Second pass during logging uses a stricter regex+model check to redact things that look like SSNs, MRNs, credit cards, and direct patient identifiers. There are false positives/negatives — we should tune on your sample data.
[18:20] Liam O'Neill: Tuning is key. Our patient IDs are alphanumeric codes that often look like normal words, so off-the-shelf NER trips. We'll provide a labeled 24-hour sample so you can tune thresholds.
[20:00] Jonas Eriksson: Perfect. For the POC benchmark we propose two days: one day synthetic high-throughput to validate throughput and batching, and one day replay of your 24h sample to validate redaction rates and latency under realistic distributions. Target goals: p95 generation latency < 250ms for small prompts (<=128 tokens) in hosted mode, and throughput 2k rps for the synthetic phase with average tokens per request around 35.
[22:40] Rachel Kim: 250ms p95 — is that realistic with network overhead? We have users in EU and US.
[24:05] Jonas Eriksson: The 250ms is for Redwood Dedicated or our optimized hosted region with batching disabled for low-latency routes. For standard hosted you might see p95 around 350-450ms depending on model. We can route EU traffic to the EU region to reduce RTT.
[26:30] Tom Wu: What's the fallback if capacity is constrained? We can't have the assistant go down.
[27:20] Maya Patel: We support graceful fallback to a smaller quantized model variant; also policy-based routing can failover to a cached response or a degraded template. We'll put those in the POC runbook.
[29:50] Sara Gomez: On the security side we need KMS integration for any persisted prompt or telemetry. We also require SSO (SAML) for console access, RBAC for logs, and audit trails that show who decrypted keys.
[32:00] Jonas Eriksson: KMS is supported — we integrate with AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys on private deployment. For the hosted POC we can do a bring-your-own-key flow using a customer-managed key in your account with limited key policy.
[33:15] Asha Iyer: If we do BYOK, what's the network topology? Do you require peering or is this SaaS egress? We need to avoid open egress of PHI.
[35:00] Maya Patel: For sensitive pilots we offer VPC peering or private link options. For an initial POC we can do a temporary peering window during the benchmark days. That keeps egress on private connectivity.
[36:40] Liam O'Neill: Good. Also re: telemetry — we want to separate operational telemetry (latency, errors) from business telemetry (prompt tokens, user ids). Can telemetry be scrubbed at the edge?
[38:15] Priya Malhotra: Yes, we can configure telemetry to redact or hash identifiers at the gateway. Redwood's tracing supports token-level counters without storing prompt text; we can emit metrics with hashed user ids and counters rather than raw prompts.
[40:00] Tom Wu: How about consent changes? If a user revokes consent, can you garbage-collect their persisted prompts?
[41:20] Jonas Eriksson: We support per-user deletion API. For the POC we'll validate a 'right-to-be-forgotten' workflow: query for user artifacts, schedule purge, and update audit log. For ephemeral mode there should be nothing to purge. For 24h TTL writes, purge is immediate by removing copies and updating logs.
[43:50] Sara Gomez: Auditing needs to show the deletion request and confirmation. Also we require immutable audit logs for access attempts for at least 1 year.
[45:10] Maya Patel: Immutable audit logs are available in Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we can ship logs to your log retention bucket with write-once policies for the POC. We'll include the log retention/preservation approach in the checklist.
[47:10] Rachel Kim: Back to benchmarks — what's the expected compute footprint for the 2k rps synthetic run? We want to understand cost and whether the Dedicated pool is necessary for the pilot.
[48:40] Jonas Eriksson: For 2k rps with small responses and batching, expect a 4-GPU cluster with optimized kernels using quantized weights to hit those throughput numbers with a medium-sized LLM. If you go with strict low-latency (<250ms) for every request, you move to a lower-batching mode and that drives compute up — 6 GPUs recommended. We'll include estimated TCO in the benchmark doc.
[50:30] Liam O'Neill: We're likely to start hosted then move to Dedicated if economics push. Are there any vendor lock-in or model format issues? We prefer open model formats (GGML, ONNX) if possible.
[52:10] Jonas Eriksson: We support standard checkpoints and conversions; the runtime handles multiple formats. No vendor lock — you can bring your own model or use Redwood-curated variants.
[52:50] Maya Patel: Okay let's align on timeline. Week of 8/23 - QuantaCare provides 24hr sample + consent policy. Week of 8/30 - Redwood runs 2-day benchmark. Week of 9/06 - review meeting with results and tuned redaction rules. Pilot go/no-go end of week 9/10 to start a 6-week pilot deployment.
[54:30] Sara Gomez: That works. A couple of compliance notes: we will want SOC2 attestation and any HIPAA adjacency notes. Can you provide the SOC2 plus how you handle ePHI?
[55:40] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and a HIPAA whitepaper. We'll also provide the POC security checklist which includes BYOK walkthrough, peering steps, retention settings, and redaction tuning guidance.
[57:10] Liam O'Neill: Great. Thanks everyone.
[57:30] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with the checklist and schedule the benchmark slot.

Meeting end.

POC success criteria (as agreed in call):
- Security: BYOK or peering during benchmark, KMS integration validated, immutable audit trail for access attempts
- Privacy: Default ephemeral mode, 24h short-term audit window, tunable PII redaction achieving >95% recall for configured PII classes after tuning
- Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms (for low-latency route) or <= 400ms for standard hosted; synthetic throughput validated at target 2k rps for baseline workload
- Operations: Right-to-be-forgotten flow validated, deletion API tested, and runbook for fallbacks during capacity events
